title: Decision Filters
hook: You don't need more discipline about late client calls. You need one rule you stop debating.
statement: Pre-commit to rules that make your choices before the choices even show up.
explainer: 'Be selective' still means weighing every option. A specific rule like 'no calls after 5pm' kills most options instantly, so you decide once instead of every time.
sop: Pick a category of decisions you keep making: yeses, purchases, projects.
Write one specific rule that pre-decides it.
Count your Options and score your Filter strength from 1 to 10.
Post the rule somewhere you'll see it.
Stick to it for 30 days before tweaking.
equation_example: 12 Options on the table, and your Filter scores 8. 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5. A stronger filter drives effort way down. A weak filter barely cuts anything, so effort stays high even with a 'rule.'
question: Write one standing rule that would save you 20 decisions this month.
closing_statement: One enforced rule beats ten you admire.
caption:
Principle Nº 213: Decision Filters

You don't need more discipline about late client calls. You need one rule you stop debating.
